title: Self-Verified Distillation: Your Language Model Is Secretly Its Own Synthetic Data Pipeline
data_curation: Seed questions come from OpenThoughts (Guha et al., 2025), using only the question text and discarding provided answers/reasoning traces to fit a no-ground-truth setting: 53,125 math, 26,041 science, and 9,168 code questions spanning competition math, chemistry/physics, and algorithmic/code-golf problems. For each seed, the model samples n candidate solutions (temperature 0.8, top-p 0.95, max 32,768 tokens) and keeps only those passing a three-stage self-verification cascade with v repeated judge calls per stage; n controls exploration and v controls stringency. Ablations vary n in {1,4,8} and v in {no-filter,1,3,5}. A first-valid selection policy (one accepted solution per seed) outperforms an all-valid policy, which adds redundancy and overweights easy seeds. Best recipe is n=8, v=5.
curriculum: Not a focus of this paper. The method is a single-stage post-training refinement: starting from an already post-trained Qwen3 model, it performs supervised fine-tuning on the self-curated dataset, with no multi-stage ordering, RL, or warmup/anneal curriculum across stages. Training uses a fixed SFT recipe (AdamW, cosine decay) held constant across ablations so differences reflect data construction.
method: Self-Verified Distillation turns unlabeled seed questions into supervised data without external teachers, tool feedback, or ground-truth answers. Given a post-trained model p_theta, it samples n candidates per question, then filters each through a UQ-inspired multi-stage self-verifier: (1) cycle-consistency (infer the question from the answer, compare to the seed, 2 calls), (2) factuality check for factual/arithmetic/logical errors, (3) total-correctness check requiring ~95% complete solutions, each repeated v times with unanimous voting. A candidate is accepted only if it passes all stages in all judge calls; the model is then trained via SFT on accepted (question, solution) pairs. The core problem is that naive self-training reinforces the model's own mistakes; the contribution shows that strong prompt-based self-verification yields higher-precision filtering than unfiltered generations, and that decomposed multi-stage UQ verification beats a simple correctness prompt (+8.4 vs +4.9 mean delta) at equal strength.
eval_metrics: Metric is pass@1 averaged over random seeds, with validation benchmarks used for checkpoint selection and held-out test benchmarks reported. Math: validation MATH500, OlympiadBench-Math, AIME24 (x10), AIME25 (x10); test AIME26 (x10), HMMT 02/25 (x10). Science: validation JEEBench (x3), OlympiadBench-Physics; test GPQA Diamond (x3), HLE (x3). Coding: validation LiveCodeBench v2 (5/2023-5/2024, x6); test LCBv5 Official (8/2024-1/2025, x6), LCBv6 Official (1/2025-4/2025, x6). Compared against the UQ-TTC test-time-compute baseline (same n=8, v=5 verification at inference, up to 168 inference calls per test problem). Gains transfer across Qwen3-0.6B/4B/8B, strongest at 4B and weakest/least consistent at 0.6B (HLE regresses).
key_results: Qwen3-4B aggregate held-out pass@1 gains: +16.7 math (AIME26+HMMT), +11.1 science (GPQA Diamond+HLE), +8.3 coding (LCBv5+LCBv6); e.g. AIME26 59.3->69.3 (+10.0), HMMT 39.3->46.0 (+6.7), GPQA Diamond 50.8->60.4 (+9.6). Self-Verified Distillation beats UQ-TTC on 5 of 6 benchmark comparisons while using a single inference call at test time (vs up to 168).
evolution_note: Builds on self-improvement/self-distillation line (STaR, Quiet-STaR, Huang 2022) and adapts the Unsolved Questions benchmark's oracle-free compound validators from evaluation to post-training data construction; it explicitly contrasts with Simple Self-Distillation (Zhang 2026), which trains on raw unverified outputs. In the 2026 context it shows prompt-based self-verification can make self-generated data reliable enough to further refine already post-trained models without teachers or tools, motivating future work on matching seed-question difficulty to model capability and stronger mitigations against reinforcing systematic errors.
